name: reachability
author: fcd76f91
description: Answers yes or no: does any path exist from a source node to a target node? Use it for questions like 'Can you get from X to Y at all?', 'Is Y reachable from X?' or 'Are X and Y connected?'. Uses breadth-first search. On directed graphs (e.g. airports) it follows edge directions by default, so A->B reachable does not imply B->A; set ignore_direction=true to treat edges as two-way. Works on undirected graphs too; edge weights are ignored. Returns reachable (true/false), the number of hops on the shortest witness path and that path as a list of nodes (id and label); when unreachable, how many nodes the source can reach. Needs node ids: call lookup_node first to turn names into ids.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

source.description: Id of the start node, e.g. 'MAA'. Use lookup_node to find it from a name.

target.description: Id of the node to reach, e.g. 'LIS'. Use lookup_node to find it from a name.

ignore_direction.description: Only for directed graphs: true treats every edge as two-way (asks whether the nodes are connected at all).
